name: SZA
label: Top Dawg Entertainment / RCA
lede: A marine biology dropout who borrowed beats off the internet, waited five years between albums, and then made one that Pitchfork ranked No. 1 of 2023.

eras.title: A marine biology major with a laptop
eras.text: Solána Rowe grew up in New Jersey and studied marine biology. Then a friend handed a few of her songs to the right person at Top Dawg Entertainment, and the science career stopped mattering.

years.h: Born in St. Louis, raised in Maplewood, New Jersey
years.p: Solána Imani Rowe's mother was an AT&T executive, her father a CNN video producer; she went to Sunday school and Muslim school both.

years.h: Marine biology at Delaware State, until the last semester
years.p: SZA left Delaware State University in her final semester, then took jobs including bartending and dancing to support herself.
years.xp: The name came later. According to Wikipedia, SZA comes from the Supreme Alphabet of the Five Percent Nation: S for savior or sovereign, Z for Zig-Zag, A for Allah. The shape of it also echoes RZA and GZA of [[Wu-Tang Clan|0febdcf7-4e1f-4661-9493-b40427de2c13]].

years.h: A boyfriend's clothing brand, a Kendrick Lamar show, a friend with a demo
years.p: At CMJ 2011 her boyfriend's clothing company sponsored a show featuring [[Kendrick Lamar|381086ea-f511-4aba-bdf9-71c753dc5077]]; a friend passed her tracks to TDE president Terrence "Punch" Henderson, who liked them and stayed in touch.
years.xp: Nothing was signed that night. Per Wikipedia's account, Punch kept in contact, and she signed with TDE two years later.

years.h: See.SZA.Run: beats borrowed off the internet
years.p: A self-released, 24-minute EP made with a neighbor and, in her words, beats stolen off the internet.
years.xp:
SZA has said she recorded it with a nearby friend using production apps and internet beats, with no plan for it to be a career. Producers credited include brandUn DeShay and AP Super; working with DeShay led to more formal collaborations.

Complex called it made for multiple listens. The Guardian's Paul Lester compared her to Drake, The Weeknd, Miguel and Frank Ocean, calling her "the female version" of them.

years.cap: SZA performing at the Grand National Tour · Wikimedia
years.h: Top Dawg signs SZA, the label's first woman
years.p: She joins a roster that already includes [[Kendrick Lamar|381086ea-f511-4aba-bdf9-71c753dc5077]] and [[Schoolboy Q|bce6d667-cde8-485e-b078-c0a05adea36d]], two years after Punch first heard her tracks.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the signing to July 14, 2013. Her second EP, S, had come out that April, three months earlier.

eras.title: Z, then the long wait
eras.text: A ten-song TDE debut, songs written for other people, and a first album that was promised for 2015 and did not show up.

years.h: Z: Kendrick and Chance the Rapper on the guest list
years.p: Ten songs, with production from [[Mac Miller|a0e8a1b1-5f8f-475a-a253-17415c17d0ff]], Emile Haynie and Toro y Moi. Pitchfork gave it 5.9.
years.xp:
"Babylon" with Kendrick Lamar was the lead single, its video set in swampy baptismal waters. Chance the Rapper guests on "Child's Play" and TDE labelmate [[Isaiah Rashad|37547347-ea75-45fa-9766-ff36b44d8147]] on "Warm Winds".

Wikipedia reports it debuted at No. 39 on the Billboard 200 with 6,980 copies and had sold more than 26,000 in the US in total. Metacritic averaged 66 from 15 reviews.

years.h: Co-writes Nicki Minaj and Beyoncé's "Feeling Myself"
years.p: Wikipedia dates the co-write to 2014, the first of several songs she wrote for bigger names while her own record waited.

years.h: The album promised for late 2015 is not late 2015
years.p: Ctrl was announced for the end of 2015, then early 2016, and missed both.
years.xp: She co-wrote "Ok Alright" for [[Travis Scott|e4a51f17-a57b-47b1-b37b-f552d0f8e9e6]] in 2015 during the wait. Ctrl itself was recorded from 2014 to 2017, across multiple studios.

years.h: A song built for her album goes to Rihanna's Anti
years.p: "Consideration" began as a SZA track called "LouAnne Johnson" meant for Ctrl; TDE reassigned it to [[Rihanna|73e5e69d-3554-40d8-8516-00cb38737a1c]].
years.xp: Wikipedia lists it among her 2016 songwriting credits, alongside the earlier co-writes with Beyoncé and Nicki Minaj. It is the one that started life as her own.

eras.title: Ctrl takes over
eras.text: Three years after Z, the debut album lands at No. 3 and refuses to leave the chart. A Black Panther single follows, and the Grammy nominations arrive.

years.h: "Drew Barrymore" is the first Ctrl single
years.p: Its video features the actual Drew Barrymore.

years.big: A kind of blinding paralysis brought on by anxiety
years.h: The label takes her hard drive
years.p: SZA's stated reason, per Wikipedia, for years of delays. In spring 2017 her label confiscated her hard drive to finish the album from roughly 150 to 200 recorded tracks.
years.xp: Wikipedia also notes that she signed with RCA Records in April 2017, two months before release.

yt: Love Galore ft. Travis Scott, official video
years.h: Ctrl: No. 3 on the Billboard 200 and a very long stay
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.4; it opened with 60,000 units and, by February 2025, had spent 400 weeks on the chart.
years.xp:
Guests include Kendrick Lamar on "Doves in the Wind", Travis Scott on "Love Galore" and Isaiah Rashad on "Pretty Little Birds". Producers include Carter Lang, ThankGod4Cody, Scum and Craig Balmoris. Metacritic averaged 87 from 17 reviews.

Time put it at the top of its year-end ranking, per Wikipedia. It is the second longest-charting R&B album by a woman.

years.cap: Cover art of Black Panther: The Album
years.h: "All the Stars" with Kendrick Lamar, from Black Panther
years.p: Lead single of the soundtrack that Ryan Coogler asked Lamar to produce; it peaked at No. 7 on the Hot 100.
years.xp:
It earned four Grammy nominations, including Record of the Year and Song of the Year, plus Oscar and Golden Globe nominations for Best Original Song. Reviews split: Rolling Stone's Jon Blistein called SZA's vocal "enthralling"; Pitchfork's Sheldon Pearce called the song "generic".

The video, from Dave Meyers and the Little Homies, has passed 583 million YouTube views as of September 2025, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Five Grammy nominations, including Best New Artist, no wins
years.p: Ctrl's Best Urban Contemporary Album nod was among them; the 60th Grammys sent her home empty-handed.

eras.title: Free SZA
eras.text: The second album was announced as imminent in 2019 and arrived in December 2022. In between: a fan hashtag, a public wobble with the label, and a Grammy from a pop hit.

years.h: SOS is coming "soon as fuck"
years.p: That was SZA's own promise in August 2019. The album came out three years and four months later.

years.big: At this point y'all gotta ask Punch.
years.h: #FreeSZA and a deleted tweet about the boss
years.p: SZA, in a tweet she later deleted, per Wikipedia, as fans campaigned for the album under #FreeSZA.
years.xp:
She followed up by saying Punch had only ever told her "soon" about release dates. Wikipedia says she later revealed that her relationship with her label had been hostile since the delays.

She also pushed back on the hashtag itself: she wasn't being held hostage, she said, and "sometimes no is a blessing."

years.h: "Good Days" lands on Christmas Day and hits No. 9
years.p: It is her first top 10 as a lead artist on the Hot 100.
years.xp:
She started it on producer Carter Lang's birthday, December 11, 2018, and "finished it randomly" in 2020. [[Jacob Collier|1df15ee0-b52b-4315-9cb9-bc5a27a685e9]] co-wrote it and cameos in the video, which SZA directed, as the man in the green television.

Pitchfork ranked it No. 20 on its 100 best songs of 2021.

years.h: "Kiss Me More" with Doja Cat wins her first Grammy
years.p: The Planet Her lead single reached No. 3 on the Hot 100; at the 2022 Grammys it won Best Pop Duo/Group Performance, the first win for both artists.
years.xp: It interpolates the melody of Olivia Newton-John's "Physical", so Steve Kipner and Terry Shaddick share songwriting credit. Warren Fu directed the video, which puts both singers on a planet of aliens.

years.h: The cover: a yacht, a St. Louis Blues jersey, Princess Diana
years.p: SZA wears a modified St. Louis Blues jersey, in a shot that references a Princess Diana photo from Portofino, Italy.
years.xp: "I pulled the Diana reference because I just loved how isolated she felt," SZA said. Art director Jass Bell designed the jersey.

years.src: SOS (SZA album) - Wikipedia · SZA - SOS - Reviews - Album of The Year
years.h: SOS: 23 tracks, three guests, one Ol' Dirty Bastard sample
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.7 and Best New Music; it opened at No. 1 with 318,000 units.
years.xp:
SZA asked around for features and got verses from only three people: [[Don Toliver|a0723a3c-4135-438e-85c5-012712144ede]], [[Phoebe Bridgers|96855c21-b832-4366-ba12-0d2330c36a86]] and Travis Scott. Producers include Babyface, Benny Blanco, Rodney Jerkins and DJ Dahi, with ThankGod4Cody co-producing seven tracks. It samples the late Ol' Dirty Bastard.

Metacritic averaged 90 from 20 reviews. The Observer, at 60, was the outlier; it found a fine line between versatility and no cohesion.

eras.title: The year SOS wouldn't leave
eras.text: An album from the previous December turns into the story of the year: a video, a tour, a No. 1 single and Pitchfork's top spot.

years.src: Kill Bill (song) - Wikipedia · SOS (SZA album) - Wikipedia
years.h: "Kill Bill" gets a video with Vivica A. Fox in it
years.p: Christian Breslauer directed; Fox, who starred in the Tarantino films, has a cameo.
years.xp: Breslauer said of Quentin Tarantino, "Tarantino is the ultimate chop and screw hybrid filmmaker in how he grabs from so many films and genres." The song gave SZA her first No. 1 on the Hot 100 and later spent 21 weeks at No. 1 on Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs, per Wikipedia.

years.h: The SOS Tour runs from February 2023 to May 2024
years.p: Omar Apollo opens, and Raye joins for the European dates.

years.h: "Snooze" becomes a single and charts all 52 weeks of 2023
years.p: It later won Best R&B Song at the 2024 Grammys.

years.src: Pitchfork: The 50 Best Albums of 2023 - Year-End Lists · SOS (SZA album) - Wikipedia · SZA - SOS - Reviews - Album of The Year
years.h: Pitchfork ranks SOS No. 1 of 2023, ahead of Caroline Polachek
years.p: Pitchfork's 8.7 had already tagged it Best New Music; its top five put [[Caroline Polachek|d8f43dc5-4613-48ac-8c23-a62b82f8c67a]] second and [[Billy Woods|f30fea51-fa9c-4067-bc49-fc43236e89ba]] with Kenny Segal third.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's list has SOS at 1, Desire, I Want to Turn Into You at 2, Maps at 3, Wednesday's Rat Saw God at 4 and Nourished by Time's Erotic Probiotic 2 at 5. Wikipedia adds that Rolling Stone, the Los Angeles Times and the Philadelphia Inquirer also put it first.

Album of the Year averages 25 critic scores at 85, with NME and The Telegraph at 100 and The Observer at 60.

eras.title: Lana, Luther and stadiums
eras.text: Nine Grammy nominations for SOS, a deluxe reissue, a Super Bowl halftime slot and a record-setting tour with Kendrick Lamar.

years.src: SOS (SZA album) - Wikipedia · Kill Bill (song) - Wikipedia
years.h: Nine Grammy nominations for SOS, one album win
years.p: It lost Album of the Year to Taylor Swift's Midnights and won Best Progressive R&B Album.
years.xp: "Kill Bill" was nominated for Record of the Year, Song of the Year and Best R&B Performance, per Wikipedia. Rolling Stone later put it at No. 267 on its 500 greatest songs.

years.h: "Luther" with Kendrick Lamar, off GNX
years.p: It debuted at No. 3 and reached No. 1 on March 1, 2025, for 13 straight weeks.
years.xp: At the 68th Grammys it won Record of the Year and Best Melodic Rap Performance, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Lana: SOS gets 15 more songs
years.p: The deluxe reissue adds "Saturn" and "Drive", among others, and sends SOS back to No. 1 in 2025.
years.xp: A further reissue on February 9, 2025 added four more tracks, per Wikipedia.

years.cap: SZA performing "Nobody Gets Me" in London during the Grand National Tour · Wikimedia
yt: Super Bowl halftime with Kendrick Lamar
years.h: SZA joins Kendrick Lamar at the Super Bowl LIX halftime show
years.p: They first performed "Luther" live there.

years.h: Grand National Tour: 47 shows, $390.7 million
years.p: Wikipedia lists it as the highest-earning rap tour ever; SZA played the North American and European dates.
years.xp: Mustard opened; 2.037 million tickets sold. She launched her makeup line, Not Beauty, through tour pop-ups and posted behind-the-scenes vlogs from the road.
